# TurnOver 2.0, build 22.4
### Fixed
- Open and Save dialogs are read: a file dialog in TextEdit, or "browse for file" on a web page in Safari. macOS draws them in a separate service, which TurnOver ignored as a process that isn't an application; the service serving the app in front now counts as that app. Reported by Maldalain (issue 14). - After the Mac wakes and is unlocked, TurnOver takes over again when the swap is off. TurnOver turns VoiceOver on for the lock screen, which it can't read; with the swap off it then never turned VoiceOver off again, so VoiceOver stayed in charge after every wake until it was turned off by hand. A VoiceOver that was already on before the Mac slept stays on. Reported by the maintainer. - App Store: Return on a search result opens it. The results page's container reports no size, so every row counted as off screen and Return said "could not reach … try again" for an app plainly on screen; the page's list, or the window, now gives the area, and a page with no scroll bar asks the row to scroll into view. Search results that arrive in stages (11, then 24, then 36 for "water") are read again as they settle, the place kept by name, and the Store's own hit test, which lags a new results page, is given up to a second to agree before the icon is clicked. Reported by the maintainer (Keynote, from a search for Pages; then the water apps). - VO-Left and VO-Right can move past segmented controls, such as the buttons in a SwiftUI picker, without getting trapped between their segments. - Finder's desktop: each item says its own place ("3 of 35"), not "35 of 35" for every one. Reported by jcast77 (issue 140). - TurnOver Key: pressing Command Control Period again just after "TurnOver off" no longer leaves the key doing nothing until its helper restarts (a contributor's change). - An app that refuses TurnOver's notification sign-ups as it comes forward (Telegram from the Mac App Store) no longer holds TurnOver up for seconds: the second try runs off the main thread, as the first one does (a contributor's change). - Windows style: Option D, which opens the Desktop folder, no longer leaves TurnOver silent while macOS asks for permission to the Desktop folder (a contributor's change). - Copy VoiceOver settings reads a VoiceOver export that stores its voice the newer, flattened way; it failed with "no voice" for such an export (a contributor's change). - Pages: a document just opened can be read with the arrows. Pages reported its page layout as the focus, with no caret in it; the body text takes the focus instead (a contributor's change). - Next and previous item reach the texts between the buttons of a System Settings pane, which said "nothing to review" at every press (a contributor's change). - JAWS keys do what JAWS's do: Caps Lock Apostrophe, Option Caps Lock X, Caps Lock V and Caps Lock F3 have their JAWS meanings rather than the Windows style's keys underneath; Caps Lock F7, F6 and F5 list a page's links, headings and form fields; and Caps Lock Left and Right Arrow stay the previous and next item in a text field (a contributor's changes). - Clicks are made as a hand makes them, the pointer there first and the button held a moment, so a dialog that ignored a quick click (Bambu Studio's) takes it. - Turning VoiceOver on uses VoiceOver's own shortcut first, which is quicker, and opens VoiceOver only if that fails. - The TurnOver layer's K changes the keyboard style without TurnOver stepping in where VoiceOver leads, and the new style's name is said once, not by both readers. - The spoken Tab hint in password fields is gone: it got in the way of moving around. - Settings: the Experimental group is a plain section; its disclosure triangle wouldn't open from the keyboard. - The control channel between TurnOver, its Settings window and TurnOver Key keeps every message whole under load, and a late reply can no longer reach the wrong client (a contributor's change). - Plugins from the library: an archive that expands well beyond its stated size, or holds files its listing doesn't show, is refused (a contributor's change). - Speech: when TurnOver's voice never starts as it is needed (the system voice stuck), VoiceOver is given the speech back instead of staying muted. Issue 71. - Starting TurnOver waits until its keyboard access is really working before it mutes VoiceOver, so a start can't leave keys unheard. Issue 52. - Moving by character keeps a letter or emoji made of several parts whole, in text fields and in Terminal. Issues 159 and 180. - Searching a window for the next heading, link or control no longer holds TurnOver up, and results that arrive after you've moved to another app are dropped. Issue 119. - App Store: pages are read in the page's own order, the first content is read before shelves further down finish loading, a late page load can no longer move the selection or act on an old row, and confirming a purchase needs a fresh press of its own. Issues 54, 173, 174 and 176. - Music, Podcasts and TV: pages are read one at a time and a late read is dropped, the selection stays on the same item when the page refreshes, and actions go to the window you're in. Issue 182. - TV: choosing Home in the sidebar goes to Home's page instead of staying on Search, and shelves are read as soon as they're ready. Issue 186. - Word: page reading checks that the window and the page range are still current, and Word's own sound at the start or end of the text is left to Word, so it isn't heard twice. Issue 178. - Mail: a message is read even when it sits beside an editable reply area. Issue 179. - Safari: a late reply from Find or a tab switch is no longer spoken after you've moved on. Issue 181. - Speech recovery: a voice queue still stuck after sleep or wake-up grace gets another recovery attempt. A late replacement cannot overwrite a player that has recovered or been replaced, and restarting waits at most two seconds for its spoken warning, even if the system voice is stuck too. Issue 155. - Privacy: typed keys and braille cells are kept out of diagnostic logs, braille typing echo stays out of speech history, and deleting a pending braille cell in a password field does not speak it. Helper diagnostics no longer keep page titles or element text. Feedback reports remove old input and helper diagnostics even when speech is included. Issues 60, 61, 62 and 68.

# TurnOver 2.0, build 22.3
### Fixed
- Typing echo: after a Backspace, the word said at the next space was the word before the one just typed when the field was slow to take the space (TextEdit, WhatsApp). The field's word now counts only once the space is in; until then TurnOver looks again, and after a tenth of a second says the letters typed. - JAWS keys: Caps Lock H reads the sentence, as in JAWS; it opened the Speech settings (a contributor's change).

# TurnOver 2.0, build 22.2
### Fixed
- After the Mac wakes and is unlocked, TurnOver comes back. The lock turns VoiceOver on for the login window; the notice of that arrived only after the wake, minutes later, and TurnOver took it for VoiceOver turned on by hand, so it stayed off until quit and started again. The lock's own VoiceOver no longer counts, and once secure input is off TurnOver looks again for up to ten seconds until an ordinary app is in front. - TurnOver Settings: Tab and Shift Tab are TurnOver's own in its window: the sidebar, then the section's controls in screen order, round and round, whatever the Mac's Keyboard navigation setting says. With that setting off (the Mac's default) the window's own Tab reached the sidebar and the ducking pop-up and nothing else, and TurnOver's generic Tab fallback, sorting the sidebar by its middle, skipped the top half of the pane. Reported by four people on AppleVis; reproduced here with the setting off and on. - Copying VoiceOver's settings with a Siri voice chosen in VoiceOver no longer sounds like a failure: the copy is reported, then that the voice is a Siri voice, which Apple gives to Siri and VoiceOver alone, so TurnOver keeps its own, with where to choose another. Reported on AppleVis. - NVDA and JAWS keys: Left Option on its own, when the Dock doesn't take the focus (macOS's own Move focus to the Dock shortcut turned off), says so and where to turn it on, instead of nothing. Reported on AppleVis. - The shortcut menu (VO-Shift-M; Shift F10 or Right Option in the NVDA and JAWS styles) opens the menu of the item TurnOver is on: its own menu action where it has one, else a right click in the middle of it. Control Return, the fallback before, opened nothing in Finder or Safari, and on one Mac the desktop's menu instead of the item's. With no item, TurnOver says so. Reported on AppleVis. - VoiceOver keys: after VO-Shift-Down into Safari's toolbar, VO-Right moves along it and bumps at its end. Safari sends the focus TurnOver had put on the button back to the page, and the cursor followed it there: VO-Right then bumped at once, or landed on the window's close button. Issue 106. - A password field says, once a run, that Tab or Shift Tab leaves it: macOS keeps every key from TurnOver in a password field, so VO-Left and VO-Right can't. Issue 107. - WhatsApp: Return on a conversation checks that it is the one now open before going to its message box. WhatsApp answered the press with success and kept the conversation already open, so a link pasted and sent went to the wrong person. On a mismatch the row is selected instead; if that fails too, TurnOver says which conversation is open and stays in the list. - Spotlight on macOS 27 is read: Command Space says the search field, the letters typed go to it, Tab reaches the microphone, Escape says it closed (Urh's change; Spotlight's panel is drawn by "Siri AI" there, which TurnOver didn't follow). Reported on AppleVis.
